Genuine: dependency-graph list scheduler packing VLIW slots, 32 vectors of 8 lanes, three hash stages fused into multiply-adds, tree levels 0 to 4 held in registers and chosen by vselect, scalar gathers below. Tree and input values are read from memory at run time and the tuned CFG only sets schedule priorities, so any random tree and inputs of this shape work. It relies on every index starting at 0 (Input.generate guarantees it, so the wrap-around is static), asserts forest_height 10 and rounds 16, and never writes the final indices, which the upstream test does not check (its index assertion is commented out upstream).

Genuine: list scheduler with register allocation, vectorised hash with three stages fused into multiply-add, preloaded top levels picked with vselect on the flow engine, the final hash XOR folded into those node constants, spare vector work spread over scalar ALUs. VEC_BIAS and the vselect table are schedule priorities found by a local search; the cycle count does not depend on the data. Tree pointers are read from the memory header. Same two assumptions as the others: all indices start at 0 and the final indices are not written back.

Genuine: vectorised hashing, the first three tree levels cached in vectors (level one as an affine function of the index), VLIW scheduling. Tree values are loaded from memory at run time. It hard-codes the 7-word memory header when computing base addresses, starts every index at 0 by broadcast rather than loading it, and does not write the final indices; all of that holds for any random input of this shape.
